<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*Four soldiers are killed during a raid at a house in north [[Lebanon]] in pursuit of a militant wanted in connection with a fatal shooting last month. The militant is killed during the raid, and is identified as Khaled al-Talawi, a former [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|Islamic State]] member who formed a splinter terrorist cell. [https://www.reuters.com/article/lebanon-crisis-security-int-idUSKBN2650GL (Reuters)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2020 Atlantic hurricane season]]
**[[Hurricane Sally]] [[rapid intensification|rapidly intensifies]] into a strong [[Category 1 hurricane]], and is expected to make landfall near the [[Louisiana]]-[[Mississippi]] border as a strong Category 2 hurricane. [https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/text/refresh/MIATCDAT4+shtml/141631.shtml? (National Hurricane Center)]
**Governor of Louisiana [[John Bel Edwards]] declares a [[state of emergency]] for [[New Orleans]] and other parts of the state as it is expected that Hurricane Sally will make landfall as a strong hurricane on Tuesday. [https://edition.cnn.com/2020/09/14/us/tropical-storm-sally-louisiana-monday/index.html (CNN)]
**[[Hurricane Paulette]] makes landfall on [[Bermuda]] as a high-end Category 1 hurricane. [https://www.foxnews.com/world/bermuda-hurricane-paulette-eye-weather-storm-island-tropical-atlantic-hurricane-season (Fox News)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
***The [[United Arab Emirates]] approves [[China National Pharmaceutical Group|Sinopharm]]'s vaccine for frontline workers following successful [[Phase III clinical trials]] in [[Abu Dhabi]]. The [[World Health Organization|WHO]]-recognized trial began on July 16 and involved 31,000 volunteers. [https://www.thenational.ae/uae/health/coronavirus-uae-authorises-emergency-use-of-vaccine-for-frontline-workers-1.1077680 (''The National'')]

;International relations
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on politics]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania]]
**President of Palau [[Tommy Remengesau Jr.]] announces he will be hosting an in-person meeting with the leaders of [[Kiribati]], [[Nauru]], the [[Federated States of Micronesia]] and the [[Marshall Islands]]. Nauru's President [[Lionel Aingimea]] says the leaders agreed to attend Palau's Independence Day on October 1 as the five Pacific countries remain free of COVID-19. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/426010/palau-to-host-in-person-micronesian-leaders-summit (RNZ)]
*[[China–United States relations]]
**The [[Embassy of the United States, Beijing]] says [[Terry Branstad]] is expected to leave his post as [[List of ambassadors of the United States to China#List of ambassadors to the People's Republic of China|U.S. Ambassador to China]] in early October. No reason is given for the move and no replacement has been announced. China says it was not notified. [https://www.scmp.com/news/china/diplomacy/article/3101485/china-us-tension-ambassador-china-terry-branstad-stepping-down (SCMP)]

;Law and crime
*''[[Connecticut v. ExxonMobil Corp.]]''
**[[Connecticut Attorney General]] [[William Tong]] files a lawsuit against [[ExxonMobil]] for their products contributing to the emissions that cause [[Climate change|global warming and climate change]]. [https://ctmirror.org/2020/09/14/tong-takes-on-exxonmobil-over-climate-change/ (CTMirror)]
*Aftermath of the [[Duma arson attack]]
**Amiram Ben-Uliel, an [[Israelis|Israeli]] terrorist who killed a [[Palestinians|Palestinian]] couple and their 18-month-old son during a racially-motivated [[arson]] attack in [[Duma, Nablus|Duma]], [[Nablus Governorate|Nablus]], [[West Bank]] in 2015, is sentenced to [[life imprisonment]] by an Israeli court. [https://ca.reuters.com/article/topNews/idCAKBN2652BN (Reuters)]
*A man is in a [[coma]] after he was hit by a [[Victoria Police|police]] car and kicked in the head by an officer during an arrest in [[Melbourne]], [[Australia]]. Prior to the incident, the victim was being treated at a hospital for mental health issues. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-australia-54146225 (BBC)]
*A court in [[Rwanda]] charges [[Paul Rusesabagina]], who inspired the film ''[[Hotel Rwanda]]'', with 12 counts, including "terrorism, complicity in murder and forming or joining an armed group", among other charges. Rusesabagina, a strong critic of President [[Paul Kagame]], did not respond to an offer of a plea. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/09/hotel-rwanda-hero-paul-rusesabagina-charged-terrorism-200914090417473.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 Liberal Democratic Party (Japan) leadership election]]
**[[Yoshihide Suga]] wins a ruling [[Liberal Democratic Party (Japan)|Liberal Democratic Party]] leadership election, paving the way for him to become [[Prime Minister of Japan|Prime Minister]] in a parliamentary vote this week. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-japan-politics-results/japans-suga-wins-ruling-party-leadership-race-to-replace-abe-idUSKBN2650P1 (Reuters)]
*[[Libyan Civil War (2014–present)|Second Libyan Civil War]]
**The [[Tobruk]]-based [[House of Representatives (Libya)|House of Representatives]] resigns amid violent protests in eastern [[Libya]] over deteriorating living conditions and corruption. A spokesman for [[Field marshal (Libya)|Field Marshal]] [[Khalifa Haftar]], who is the ''de facto'' leader of eastern Libya, says the administration supports peaceful protests but would not allow "terrorists and the [[Muslim Brotherhood]]" to hijack them. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-54145499 (BBC)]

;Science and technology
*[[Climate change in the Arctic]]
**Satellite imagery shows that a big chunk of ice shattered into many small pieces from the last remaining [[ice shelf]] in [[Nioghalvfjerdsfjorden]], [[Greenland]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/science-environment-54127279 (BBC)]
**The discovery of the perfectly preserved remains of a [[cave bear]], believed to be 22,000 to 39,500 years old ([[Late Pleistocene]]), is made in [[Lyakhovsky Islands]], [[Siberia]] in the thawing [[permafrost]]. [https://apnews.com/577b29734cb7ce40518eac6a5303cfb4 (AP)]
*[[Life on Venus]]
**The [[Jane Greaves]]-led international scientific team announce that they have detected a gas called [[phosphine]] in the [[Atmosphere of Venus|atmosphere]] of [[Venus]] that indicates [[microorganism]]s may inhabit [[Earth]]'s inhospitable neighbor. If confirmed, it would be the first known [[extraterrestrial life]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-space-exploration-venus/potential-sign-of-alien-life-detected-on-inhospitable-venus-idUSKBN2652GO (Reuters)]
